A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AB-MCTS work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on LiveCodeBench, CodeContest, ARC-AGI, and three MLE-Bench competitions, including performance and search-behavior analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds sensitivity studies, progressive-widening comparisons, and original ARC-AGI-2 experiments.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix B already proposes multi-LLM search with global generator selection after choosing an expansion node. v4 retains this as Algorithm I and adds Algorithm II, using a GEN node per LLM and local comparisons during tree traversal (D.1.3). This extends generator selection while retaining the single-LLM algorithms.

E1.justification: v4 adds ARC-AGI-2 evaluation, extending the existing grid-transformation reasoning coverage to a harder benchmark. The original four benchmarks and three MLE-Bench competitions remain.

E2.justification: Progressive widening, previously only discussed, is evaluated at three parameter settings against AB-MCTS in v4 Table 4. The original main comparison methods remain; Appendix D additionally compares multi-LLM search with AB-MCTS-A using individual LLMs.

E3.justification: New protocols include 16-call GPT-4o prior-sensitivity experiments, a 128-call progressive-widening comparison using deepseek-v3-0324, and branching factors 3, 5, and 10. ARC-AGI-2 uses 120 problems, 250 calls, three reasoning models, Pass@k coverage, and preliminary rule-based Pass@2 selection. ARC-AGI also gains Pass@1 evaluation; the original main settings are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds prior sensitivity, progressive-widening parameter comparisons, fixed-branching-factor ablations, Pass@1/Pass@2 comparisons, and node-degree distributions. Model-allocation analysis and cross-model correction examples further extend the original width/depth plots and MLE-Bench search-tree cases (A.6, C.4–C.8, D.2.3).

E5.justification: v4 adds ± uncertainty values to the retained Table 1 means and explicitly reports five-run means and standard deviations for Table 3. The original benchmark run counts and Figure 4's 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged; no increase in the original run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their means and rankings, while Tables 3–6 and Appendix D add substantial results. The new progressive-widening experiment reports 51.8 for AB-MCTS-A (Beta) versus 50.7 for the best widening configuration under deepseek-v3-0324, rather than a same-setting improvement over Table 1. ARC-AGI-2 reports approximately 23% coverage for o4-mini repeated sampling, 27.5% for single-LLM AB-MCTS, over 30% for multi-LLM search, and preliminary Pass@2 of 19.2%.

T1.justification: The mixed-model assumptions and Gaussian/Beta update rules are retained after matching moved and renumbered equations. Main-text formalization largely restates existing mathematics; notation corrections, walkthroughs, and explanation of the standard progressive-widening rule introduce no substantive new derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: adaptive unbounded branching combines exploration with refinement, with two principal AB-MCTS variants and advantages over repeated sampling and standard MCTS.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations of AB-MCTS-A's preference for wider trees, guidance on quality/runtime tradeoffs, and interpretations of parameter robustness and model collaboration. D.3 identifies final-answer selection as a practical bottleneck. However, C.6's new assertion that metric rankings remain unchanged contradicts Table 5, where the Gaussian and Beta variants reverse their mean ordering.

D1.justification: v4 adds TreeQuest code-access information, explains the final three-node MCTS expansion needed to meet the 128-call limit, and documents model identifiers, temperature, and answer selection for the new experiments. Existing PyMC listings, default priors, data-processing details, and H100 execution information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 distinguishes the LATS coding configuration from RAP, SWE-Search, and RepoUnderstander instead of treating them collectively as the experimental baseline. Progressive-widening positioning is expanded; Sokota's abstraction-refinement work and multi-LLM, ARC-AGI-2, and model references are added, while the Kocsis–Szepesvari citation is removed.

P1.justification: v4 substantially expands method exposition with stepwise Thompson sampling, explicit main-text models, and complete selection/backup walkthroughs. It also reorganizes the appendices: retained experimental details and analyses move from C/D to B/C, while the expanded multi-LLM material moves from B to D.

P2.justification: v4 adds four tables and five figures covering sensitivity, comparator results, node degrees, multi-LLM performance, allocation, and collaboration. Table 1 is reformatted to accommodate uncertainty values. Original graphic content is retained, with relocation and renumbering, including the exchange of Figures 6 and 7.

improvement.justification: The progressive-widening comparison and prior/branching-factor studies address important validation gaps in v2's adaptive-search argument. Worked examples, code-access information, and empirical evaluation of the previously proposed multi-LLM extension substantially improve clarity and evidential support. D.3 usefully distinguishes search coverage from final-answer performance. The incorrect ranking-invariance statement in C.6 is a localized drawback that does not outweigh these gains.
